paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God means what He says, even when it hurts to watch. Nebuchadnezzar carried off the treasures "As the LORD had declared" (2 Kings 24:13). Nobody in Jerusalem could say they weren't warned, and the king's walls, the mighty men and the gold couldn't stop a single word God had spoken.

Now here's the part that should stick with you. Jehoiachin "did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his father had done" (2 Kings 24:9). I think that's the sneaky danger, friend: copying what you grew up around without ever stopping to ask if it's right. Habits get handed down like a family recipe, and that's great for cookies and rough for sin.

So what do you do with that? Take God's Word seriously BEFORE the siege shows up at your door. When He says something, believe it, and don't wait for the walls to come down to start listening. I know a little about being carried off to a place you didn't pick, and I can tell you the best time to trust the One who made the dough is long before the oven gets hot.
